title: NSGo game brief (version 1)
description: Brief is the root of a versioned brief.yaml file at a game project's root. The agent reads it before every request and checks its work against it, and playtests can read structured targets from Feel.Targets.

version.description: Version is the schema version; it must equal BriefVersion (1).

basis.description: Basis records where the brief's statements come from: locked (a decision only the person changes), target (an experience goal to aim for) or assumption (a default an agent may revise).

pitch.description: Pitch describes what the game is meant to be in a sentence or two.

genre.description: Genre lists the game's primary genre labels, such as "2D platformer" and "action".

tags.description: Tags lists optional extra keywords or sub-genre tags describing the game.

platforms.description: Platforms lists the target platforms and control styles, such as "desktop", "phones, touch", and "web".

artDirection.description: ArtDirection describes visual style, resolution, palette, and silhouette rules.

art.description: Art holds structured visual direction notes and pinned reference images read by the agent before every request.

toneAndAudio.description: ToneAndAudio describes mood, music, and sound direction.

feel.description: Feel describes game feel, difficulty pacing, and structured playtest targets.

changes.description: Changes records explicit edits to brief intent in deterministic order.

BriefArt.description: BriefArt holds structured art direction notes and pinned project-relative reference images.

basis.description: Basis records where the art direction comes from: locked, target or assumption.

direction.description: Direction optionally describes visual direction inline under art.direction.

references.description: References lists pinned project-relative reference images included with every agent request.

BriefArtReference.description: BriefArtReference names one pinned reference image listed under art.references in brief.yaml.

path.description: Path is the project-relative slash path to the reference image (for example "art/reference/spikes_ref.png").

note.description: Note is an optional short description of what the reference illustrates.

BriefChange.description: BriefChange records one edit to the brief's intent, listed under changes in brief.yaml.

date.description: Date is the UTC day of the edit, as YYYY-MM-DD.

field.description: Field names what changed, such as "feel.targets.floor_01.median_time".

from.description: From is the value before the edit, empty when the field was added.

to.description: To is the value after the edit, empty when the field was removed.

reason.description: Reason says why the field changed.

BriefFeel.description: BriefFeel describes game feel, difficulty expectations, and machine-readable playtest targets.

basis.description: Basis records where the feel summary comes from: locked, target or assumption.

summary.description: Summary describes target game feel, controls responsiveness, and difficulty pacing in plain language.

targets.description: Targets lists structured playtest targets readable by playtest runners and the editor.

BriefPlaytestTarget.description: BriefPlaytestTarget declares one measurable playtest target in brief.yaml's feel and difficulty section.

metric.description: Metric is the playtest metric name this target constrains, such as "median_time", "deaths", or "finished".

scene.description: Scene optionally restricts this target to a specific scene or level name, such as "floor_01".

basis.description: Basis records where this target comes from: locked (only the person changes it), target (an experience goal) or assumption (a default an agent may tune).

summary.description: Summary is an optional human-readable description of the target, such as "2–4 deaths on floor 3".

unit.description: Unit is an optional display unit, such as "s", "ms", or "%".

min.description: Min is the inclusive lower bound (value >= Min).

max.description: Max is the inclusive upper bound (value <= Max).
